PullRequest.Title: Hide Migrations page in sidebar when no available migrations
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338905

This pull request implements the feature to hide the **Migrations** page from the Customizations sidebar when there are no pending migration candidates.

### Changes
- Modified `aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts` to conditionally hide the **Migrations** sidebar entry based on the presence of pending migration candidates.
- Ensured that ignored migration groups remain accessible for restoration, even when they do not count towards the visible migration badge.
- Added regression tests in `aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts` to verify the new behavior.

### Validation
- The client build and focused unit tests have passed successfully.
- ESLint checks have been completed without issues.
- Dependency restoration was performed, and no tracked manifest changes were made. 

This change enhances the user experience by decluttering the sidebar when no migrations are available while still allowing access to ignored migrations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the AI Customizations editor or refresh migration inventory after prompt, MCP, configuration, workspace, session, or harness changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing refresh triggers are coalesced by customizationMigrationRefreshDelayer, then computeCustomizationMigrationInfo discovers candidates and target folders before setCustomizationsToMigrate refreshes the welcome page, sidebar shortcut, and dashboard. The added hasPendingMigrations predicate runs only after discovery and before the existing sidebar style/text updates and layoutSidebar call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: customizationMigrationService.computeMigration discovers candidates for each enabled migration category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four calls per effective refresh, one per enabled fixed category, launched concurrently after refresh coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-enabled-category discovery calls were already required before refreshing the sidebar and dashboard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All discovery calls must settle before sidebar candidate state is committed. The added predicate runs afterward and does not delay or multiply these calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: itemProvider.provideSourceFolders resolves migration target folders for each distinct target type.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per deduplicated target type present in discovered non-MCP candidates, launched concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deduplicated source-folder lookups were already on the refresh critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls settle before setCustomizationsToMigrate and sidebar refresh. The diff neither adds target types nor invokes the provider.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most four fixed homepage migration categories; the added predicate performs one map lookup and array-length check per category and short-circuits on the first nonempty category. Candidate count does not affect the added work because getMigrationCandidates returns the existing array when storage is omitted.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Migration discovery remains Promise.all across enabled categories (maximum four), and source-folder discovery remains Promise.all across deduplicated target types. The existing Delayer coalesces refresh requests and sequence/cancellation checks discard superseded work. The diff changes none of this concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The candidate map is populated by each completed discovery refresh and reused by the added predicate. There is no new cache or miss behavior; empty and nonempty arrays are read from the same existing map. Existing refreshes recompute discovery rather than serving a persistent cache, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed predicate and getMigrationCandidates implementation were traced directly; with no storage argument the helper performs an enablement check, map lookup, and returns the existing candidate array.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying discovery duration and event frequency vary by workspace, but the diff-added cost is deterministically bounded to four map lookups and length checks per effective refresh.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The added work is constant, tiny, and occurs after unchanged expensive discovery boundaries; it does not add an additional layout pass.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ignore or restore a migration group while retaining access to ignored pending migrations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user confirmation/quick pick and existing storage update complete, then refreshCustomizationMigrationUi synchronously rebuilds migration summaries, updates the sidebar shortcut, and renders dashboard state. The new predicate checks whether any enabled category still has candidates so the shortcut remains reachable even when all are ignored.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Four fixed categories. The added check does not enumerate candidates or inspect ignored-group storage; it checks only each existing candidate array's length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: This UI-only refresh is synchronous after the user interaction; no new task, queue, IPC, or parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: It reads the already-populated customizationsByMigrationCategory map. Ignore state storage behavior is unchanged, and the added predicate deliberately does not consult or alter it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: refreshCustomizationMigrationUi and updateSidebarMigrationShortcut are direct callers, and the changed line has no transitive boundary operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of ignore/restore interactions is user-driven, but each added check is fixed and negligible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Sidebar visibility now changes based on pending candidates using bounded in-memory work; existing synchronous layout remains one call per refresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Complete, delete, or otherwise remove the final migration candidate and hide the Migrations sidebar entry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing migration/delete operations perform their service or filesystem work, refresh candidate inventory, then updateSidebarMigrationShortcut reads the committed candidate map. The new predicate hides the entry when all four category arrays are empty.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing migration, file deletion, MCP uninstall, and subsequent candidate rediscovery update the migration inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Driven by the explicit user operation, followed by the same coalesced inventory refresh and grouped discovery calls as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same migration/deletion and rediscovery work occurred; the sidebar entry remained visible even when the resulting inventory was empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing operations determine when candidate state is available. The added visibility check executes afterward and adds no boundary latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The new work is independent of migrated/deleted item count: at most four category map lookups and length checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Migration and deletion sequencing is unchanged. Inventory refresh retains its existing coalescing, cancellation, and parallel category discovery; the local visibility predicate is synchronous after results are committed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The predicate consumes the newly committed candidate map and requires no cache invalidation or negative-cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call paths update the same candidate map and reach the changed predicate only after existing operations complete.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Boundary durations depend on provider and filesystem, but none are introduced or amplified by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The change adds a fixed local predicate and does not alter expensive operation count, concurrency, or critical-path placement.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of both changed files and all diff pages. Traced editor-open/event refresh, ignore/restore, and final-candidate removal scenarios through migration discovery, provider, filesystem/service boundaries, cache state, concurrency, and sidebar layout. The sole production change adds a fixed four-category in-memory presence check; no actionable performance issue or concrete regression fix was identified.
